evidence.quote: From {{inh|en|enm|stinky}}, {{m|enm|stynky}}, equivalent to {{af|en|stink|-y|id2=adjectival}}. Compare {{cog|nl|stinkig|t=stinky, foul, rotten}}, {{cog|nds|stinkig|t=stinking, stinky}}, {{cog|de|stinkig|t=stinky}}, {{cog|hrx|stinkich}}. Compare also {{cog|stq|stjunkerch|t=stinky}}, {{cog|fy|stjonkerich|t=stinky}}.

"having much stink," 1888, from stink (n.) + -y (2). Chaucer used stynky. Stinking as a… See origin and meaning of stinky. from Old English -ig , from Proto-Germanic *-iga- , from PIE -(i)ko- , adjectival suffix, cognate with elements in Greek -ikos , Latin -icus (see -ic ).
